children: Canada's main stock index fell to an eight-day low on Wednesday as oil and bond yields climbed and as the trade war between the United States and Canada intensified, with financial and technology shares among the biggest decliners.
ended down 216.49 points, or 0.6%, at 35,906.56, its third straight day of declines and the lowest closing level since September 1.

"I think that higher oil prices and higher bond yields — the combination is taking a toll on indices in what is historically a seasonally challenging month," said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global investment strategist at Edward Jones
Brent crude futures breached $100 a barrel to settle at their highest close since late May after Iran and the U.S. struck tankers in the biggest wave of attacks on shipping since the war began.

Benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yields reached their highest levels since 2023 after the announcement of an enlarged Treasury buyback of longer-dated bonds disappointed some investors who had wanted more.
"I think tariff uncertainty is not going away and that has some potential implications if it continues to drag on business decisions and down the road weigh on economic activity," Kourkafas said.

The United States banned a broad swath of Canadian alcoholic beverages, motorcycles and dairy products from import on Tuesday. Tariffs implemented last month hit sectors covering $20 billion, or 5%, of Canadian exports to the U.S.
Heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) lost 1.1%, industrials (.GSPTTIN) were down 1.2% and technology ended 2% lower.
fell 5.4% to a five-week low as concerns about AI-led disruption weighed on software stocks.
Gains for resource shares helped limit the TSX's decline.
added 1% and the materials group, which includes metal mining shares, was up 0.9%.
rose 1% as investors awaited key U.S. inflation data this week that could provide clues on prospects for Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
